title: Generator Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original generator workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete generator inspection checklist form for the standby or prime generator system that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The generator service coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Generator inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Generator readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This form is not a generator energy-control, energized-work, or transfer authorization. Stop for fuel leaks, exhaust or carbon-monoxide concerns, fire, heat, arcing, unexpected start, exposed moving parts, or unknown backfeed. Qualified and authorized personnel must control isolation, test conditions, affected loads, and return to automatic service under current site procedures.

sections.title: Generator inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: Generator, engine, controller, fuel system, battery, and ATS identities agree
Area is clear, ventilated, weather-protected, and free of combustible storage
Fuel, oil, coolant, exhaust, and battery areas show no active leak or damage
Guards, belts, hoses, terminals, cables, heaters, and charger are visibly intact
Air intake, radiator, louvers, exhaust path, and drainage are unobstructed
Starting battery condition and charger status are recorded by approved method
Controller status, active alarms, history, mode, and exercise schedule are captured
Fuel level, hour meter, oil, coolant, and representative standby readings are logged
ATS identity, source status, test authority, and affected loads are confirmed
Authorized run or transfer test results include load, duration, and anomalies
Noise, vibration, smoke, odor, heat, hunting, and leakage are absent or escalated
Unit is returned to the approved mode with limitations and follow-up visible

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Generator exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Fuel, oil, coolant, exhaust, or battery leak
Carbon-monoxide alarm, exhaust intrusion, or ventilation failure
Smoke, fire, abnormal heat, burning odor, or electrical arcing
Unexpected start, automatic operation, transfer, or backfeed risk
Exposed moving part, damaged guard, severe vibration, or loose component
Uncontrolled stored electrical, mechanical, thermal, or fluid energy
Critical-load interruption without site and operations authorization
Test or repair beyond the assigned qualified person's scope
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: This form is not a generator energy-control, energized-work, or transfer authorization. Stop for fuel leaks, exhaust or carbon-monoxide concerns, fire, heat, arcing, unexpected start, exposed moving parts, or unknown backfeed. Qualified and authorized personnel must control isolation, test conditions, affected loads, and return to automatic service under current site procedures.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Generator decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Standby or prime generator system identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
